subject.title: RFC: Declarative provider manifests instead of per-vendor lifecycle re-implementation

question: Should OpenClaw invest in a shared declarative provider-lifecycle SDK, beginning with one bounded provider-family pilot, or continue evolving the existing composable provider helpers case by case?
rationale: The evidence confirms existing composable provider seams but cannot determine whether their remaining duplication warrants a new long-lived public provider contract; that tradeoff is a maintainer product and compatibility decision.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow pilot
options.body: Define success criteria around one homogeneous provider family, preserve existing code hooks, and use the result to propose only proven shared manifest fields.

options.title: Continue helper-based evolution
options.body: Keep provider lifecycle ownership in plugins and add targeted shared SDK helpers only when a concrete repeated invariant is demonstrated.

options.title: Defer the abstraction
options.body: Close or park the RFC until a maintainer-backed implementation example identifies a specific missing SDK boundary.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow pilot
recommendation.body: Define success criteria around one homogeneous provider family, preserve existing code hooks, and use the result to propose only proven shared manifest fields.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available evidence connects this person to current plugin/core scope direction and prior decisions about when a missing plugin API merits core design work.
